newsitem.title: UK: Babcock up on H1 results, upbeat outlook.
newsitem.headline: Babcock up on H1 results, upbeat outlook.

text.p: Shares in Babcock International Group Plc rose on Thursday as the engineering company posted a rise in underlying first-half profits coupled with an upbeat outlook statement, analysts said.
The shares were up 7p at 70p by 1235 GMT, in active trading of more than 2.5 million shares.
Babcock's pre-tax profit before exceptionals rose to 2.7 million stg in the six months ended September 30 against 2.2 million stg in the same period last year.
Analysts pointed out that the company had recovered after making a 19.3 million stg loss in the year to March.
"Last year's second half-year was very poor, but they turned back into profit in the first half of this year, which is quite a good turnaroud," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
Chairman John Parker said the company had achieved a number of positive developments in the past six months, which included the completion of negotiations to acquire Rosyth Royal Dockyard.
"These achievements, together with the return to profitability and the ungeared balance sheet, gives the board confidence that the group is moving towards a more rewarding future," he said.
The company said the major restructuring programme in its materials handling division over the past 15 months had sucessfully restored the division and the German operation, in particular, to profit.
